charts.title: Proportionate Operational EBITDAF
charts.annotation: FY2026 is on a different basis to FY2022-FY2025 (excludes discontinued Manawa Energy & RetireAustralia). Like-for-like FY2025 is NZ$895.3m, so true FY25-to-FY26 growth is ~11%, not the ~7.8% this chart's raw YoY would imply.

charts.title: Per-Asset EBITDAF Contribution
charts.annotation: Manawa Energy and RetireAustralia were sold during FY2026 (their bars fall to a residual part-year figure, not a performance collapse); Contact Energy entered the portfolio at NZ$1,394.5m in FY2026 but is not yet a separate CSV column. charts.annotation: Dominated by unrealised portfolio revaluations, not operating performance: FY2025 was -NZ$286.3m and FY2026 +NZ$549.8m despite the underlying business improving in both years. Do not read this as an earnings trend -- use Proportionate Operational EBITDAF for that.

sections.title: Balance Sheet & Capital
sections.subtitle: Growth funded by debt and equity issuance, not distributable cash

charts.title: Shares Outstanding
charts.annotation: Repeated equity issuance to fund growth capex: 723.0m (FY22) to 999.3m (FY26), +38%. The DCF deliberately holds share count flat going forward because the capital raised and the EBITDAF growth it buys are not separable.

ebitdaf.title: Proportionate Operational EBITDAF
ebitdaf.content:
Infratil's share of each portfolio company's EBITDAF, weighted by ownership stake -- the core measure management guides on and is remunerated against. It is not consolidated revenue or EBITDA; Infratil has no meaningful group revenue line because it is an investment holding company, not an operating business.

For Infratil: FY2026's NZ$989.4m is Operational EBITDAF, which excludes the now-discontinued Manawa Energy and RetireAustralia. FY2022-FY2025 figures in this chart are Total Proportionate EBITDAF, which included those two businesses. The bases differ because of discontinued operations, not a corporate-cost redefinition. On a like-for-like continuing basis, FY2025 was NZ$895.3m and FY2026 growth was ~11.2% -- the company's own reported figure -- not the ~7.8% a naive read of the raw CSV cells (917.8 to 989.4) implies.

What to watch:

  • Whether FY2027 growth reaches the ~18% guidance midpoint (continuing basis) or falls back toward FY2026's 11.2% actual
  • CDC's growing share of the total -- it is increasingly the business
  • Corporate costs and non-capitalised development spend, both guided to grow faster than EBITDAF itself

portfolioValue.title: Portfolio Value vs Net Debt
portfolioValue.content:
Portfolio Value is Infratil's proportionate share of the fair value of every investee, the asset side of the NAV bridge. Net Debt is parent-level borrowings.

For Infratil: Portfolio value has grown from NZ$8.3bn (FY22) to NZ$20.6bn (FY26), but net debt has grown roughly 5x over the same period (NZ$622.6m to NZ$3,204.6m) as growth capex is funded by borrowing. Net debt shown here is the statutory 31-March figure; the DCF uses a restated NZ$2,987.5m after NZ$217.1m of post-balance-date Fortysouth sale proceeds.

What to watch:

  • Whether portfolio value growth continues to outpace debt growth
  • Refinancing terms -- a post-balance-date refinancing to ~NZ$2.1bn of committed facilities across 1/3/5-year tenors reduced near-term refinancing risk

assetContribution.title: Per-Asset EBITDAF Contribution
assetContribution.content:
Each portfolio company's proportionate contribution to Infratil's total EBITDAF -- the single best view of where the earnings actually come from and how concentrated they are becoming.

For Infratil: CDC Data Centres has gone from a minor contributor (NZ$38-82m in FY22) to by far the largest (NZ$220.4m in FY26, and 43% of portfolio value), carrying the portfolio's growth nearly alone. One NZ, the second-largest holding, actually declined in value over FY2026. Manawa Energy and RetireAustralia were both exited during FY2026 -- their falling contributions reflect divestment, not deteriorating performance. Contact Energy joined the portfolio in FY2026 at NZ$1,394.5m but does not yet have its own tracked contribution column.

What to watch:

  • Concentration risk: CDC is now large enough that its AI-datacentre cycle and its own cost-of-equity assumptions materially move the whole company's valuation
  • Whether One NZ, Wellington Airport and the smaller holdings stabilise or continue to soften

netParentSurplus.title: Net Parent Surplus (Statutory Profit)
netParentSurplus.content:
Infratil's IFRS bottom line, consolidating its investees and including fair-value movements on the portfolio.

For Infratil: This number is dominated by non-cash portfolio revaluations, not operating results, and swings accordingly: -NZ$286.3m in FY2025 (markdowns) to +NZ$549.8m in FY2026 (led by the CDC uplift), even though the underlying business grew in both years. Treat this as balance-sheet noise, not an earnings trend -- Proportionate Operational EBITDAF is the operating measure.

What to watch:

  • Do not extrapolate a run-rate from this line
  • Compare direction against EBITDAF and portfolio value growth, which tell the real operating story

equityAssets.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Assets
equityAssets.content:
Balance-sheet scale: total assets are almost entirely the fair value of portfolio investments; equity is assets less net debt and other liabilities.

For Infratil: Both have roughly tripled since FY22 as the portfolio has grown, funded by a mix of retained portfolio value gains, debt and repeated equity raisings.

What to watch:

  • The gap between the two lines is liabilities (mostly net debt) -- watch it widen faster than equity

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Total ordinary shares on issue.

For Infratil: Up from 723.0m (FY22) to 999.3m (FY26), +38%, funding growth capex (FY2026 proportionate capex was NZ$2,687m against NZ$919m of EBITDAF). The DCF holds share count flat for the projection period deliberately -- projecting further dilution without the incremental EBITDAF it buys would double-penalise the equity case.

What to watch:

  • Further capital raises, especially if guided FY2027 capex of NZ$3.8-4.4bn outpaces available debt capacity

dividend.title: Dividend per Share
dividend.content:
Cash distribution declared per ordinary share for the year.

For Infratil: Growing from NZ$6.75 cents-equivalent (FY24, first full year shown) to NZ$20.9 (FY26) as the portfolio matures, though the dividend remains a small fraction of look-through earnings given the scale of ongoing growth capex.

What to watch:

  • Dividend growth relative to EBITDAF growth -- a widening gap signals more retained capital going to growth capex

dcf.growth_hint: Year-1 growth = FY2027 guidance midpoint, rebased to the continuing (post-development-spend, post-corporate-cost) basis
dcf.base_sublabel: Proportionate EBITDAF less development spend, corporate costs & an estimated incentive-fee leak -- not free cash flow
